note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 212 to 248 - Park Valley, Castle Grove, Lenton Road.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in. Part of the round; see [[1881-standard-hill-part1]] for schedules 1 to 50.

**Park Valley is numbered all the way down - 25 to 1 - and Castle Grove is not.** The enumerator walks Park Valley by number and then turns into Castle Grove and writes nothing but the street, house after house, seven of them. **That is the same fault as 1911**, thirty years earlier, and it is the reason [[castle-grove-has-no-low-numbers]] cannot be settled from the census alone. Only one Castle Grove house is named at all: **The Lodge**, the coachman's.

**13 Park Valley is not in the property list.** Walter Wadsworth's household is there on the page, between 15 and 11, and there is no number 13 among the properties. Left unfiled rather than forced onto a neighbour.

**One number cannot be right.** Schedule 228 reads 21 Park Valley, but schedule 216 is already 21 and 228 sits between what the page calls 3 and 1. It is probably 2. It is left unfiled, because a number that contradicts itself is not evidence.

**Three of the largest manufacturers in Nottingham are on these pages.**

- **John Player**, 40, tobacco manufacturer employing 80 persons, at **9 Park Valley**, with his wife Ann and his son **William G Player, 15, tobacco manufacturer's assistant** - the firm that became John Player & Sons, in the house, ten years before the sons took it on. See [[john-player-at-9-park-valley]].
- **Thomas Forman**, 62, newspaper proprietor and Justice of the Peace, on **Castle Grove**, with three grown sons, two of them newspaper proprietors beside him. See [[thomas-forman-on-castle-grove]].
- **Frederic Dobson**, lace manufacturer on Castle Grove, **employing 1,140 men, women, boys and girls** - the largest figure anywhere in the round.

**Other lives worth the record's attention.** **Ellis Hyam**, clothier and outfitter, at 3 Lenton Road with a wife born in Malta and eight children born in London. **Fred Bell**, "Pastor of the Church of the People", at Brooklyn House, 21 Park Valley - and his wife **Annie J Bell**, entered in the occupation column as **Authoress**, one of very few women on these pages given a profession of her own. **Harry Wyles**, a law student in Samuel Johnson's house on Western Terrace in 1871, is head of Holly Hurst in Park Valley in 1881, a solicitor at 32.

**A child with no name.** At 19 Park Valley the Bells' month-old son is entered as **"No name"**. He is recorded exactly as written rather than left out, because a household of six is not a household of five.

**House names on these pages**: Clinton House, Brooklyn House, Stewart Cottage, Holly Hurst and Arundel House on Park Valley; The Lodge on Castle Grove; Oakhurst at 17 Lenton Road. Castle Bank at 5 Lenton Road and The Chestnuts at 5 Kenilworth Road the record already holds. **Arundel House is worth a second look**: the solicitor's wife is Arundel Preston and so is his daughter.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source. Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 212 to 248, transcribed by A. Hagues.
